policy.selection_test: Would this material be selected if its author had no connection to this course?
policy.workbench_policy: The workbench is one source among others. No result, optional example or advanced lesson is reserved a place because of its origin.
policy.literature_scope: Representative foundations and major approaches; an exhaustive survey is not claimed.
policy.writing_rule: Reuse exact suitable components from existing courses and write missing bridges. New claims require complete proofs or precise matching providers.

units.title: Fields, coordinates and physical quantities
units.topics: Scalar and vector fields; derivatives and integrals; spacetime; units; differential equations and initial data.
units.learning_outcome: Read a field equation and identify its unknowns, coordinates, dimensions and initial data.
units.proof_provider: Complete elementary derivations in this lesson; one-variable calculus is stated preparation.
units.prerequisite_scope: Real arithmetic, triples, elementary one-variable differentiation and integration.
proof_locators: Proposition 4.1 and (F1.18): multivariable path derivative
Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2: transport, support and exact data dependence
Proposition 7.1 and (F1.40): box flux and whole-space conservation
Exercises 1–8: complete solutions
units.authorship: Independent elementary course exposition; no research novelty is claimed.

units.title: Electromagnetism and gauge freedom
units.topics: Electric and magnetic fields; scalar and vector potentials; Maxwell equations; local changes of potential; observables.
units.learning_outcome: Calculate a gauge change and identify the quantities it preserves.
units.proof_provider: Complete elementary derivations in this lesson from Maxwell equations and YM-F01 calculus.
units.prerequisite_scope: YM-F01; one-variable calculus, including trigonometric differentiation and the derivative of arctangent.
proof_locators: Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 2.2: derivative identities
Propositions 3.1 and 4.1: continuity, constraints and exact potential equations
Theorems 5.1, 6.1 and 6.2: invariance, constructive converse and construction of potentials from homogeneous fields
Section 6 and Exercise 7: missing-axis period and exact family classification
Propositions 8.1 and 8.3: field wave equations and full local energy balance
Exercises 1–8: complete solutions
units.authorship: Independent elementary course exposition with scholarly source credit; no research novelty claim.

units.title: Symmetry through matrices
units.topics: Complex numbers and phases; rotations; matrix multiplication; unitary matrices; representations; global and local symmetry.
units.learning_outcome: Use explicit matrices to distinguish a symmetry action from a choice of local description.
units.proof_provider: Complete elementary receiving proofs, including the matrix specialization of RT-LIE-01 Proposition 1.1.
units.prerequisite_scope: YM-F01 and YM-F02; elementary trigonometry, addition formulas, derivatives and the unit-circle parametrization.
proof_locators: Lemma 2.1: square matrix injectivity and invertibility
Theorem 3.1: equivalent tests for unitarity
Section 4, F3.21–F3.25: exact rotations and complete Jacobi expansion
Section 5, F3.26–F3.31: equation symmetries, local product rule and frame identity
Theorem 6.1 and F3.36–F3.39: full electromagnetic covariance
Lemma 7.1 and Theorem 7.2: phase lifting and exact missing-axis gauge classes
Exercises 1–8: complete solutions
units.authorship: Independent course exposition; identified CC0 component reuse; no research novelty claim.

units.title: Lie groups and Lie algebras
units.topics: U(1), SU(2) and SU(3); tangent generators; commutators; exponential maps; invariant inner products.
units.learning_outcome: Calculate the Lie bracket in concrete examples and identify the group acting on a field.
units.proof_provider: Complete receiving proofs of matrix estimates, determinant identities, exponential and logarithm, group charts, tangents, brackets, concrete generators, coverings, connectedness and representations.
units.prerequisite_scope: YM-F01–YM-F03 and elementary real calculus, trigonometry, real exponential/logarithm and completeness of the real numbers.
proof_locators: Lemma 1.1 and F4.5–F4.10: estimates and full determinant identities
Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 3.1: convergent series, derivatives and inverse maps
Theorem 3.2: explicit charts, group operations and dimensions
Theorem 4.1 and F4.28–F4.34: tangents, left-invariant fields and commutator curve
Section 5: necessary and sufficient circle period test
Section 6, F4.36–F4.48: SU(2) coordinates and full smooth double covering
Section 7, F4.49–F4.57: SU(3) basis, all independent brackets and SU(2) embedding
Section 8: constructive connectedness and the two components of O(n)
Section 9, F4.60–F4.69: invariant metric, differentiated representations and centres
Exercises 1–8: complete solutions
units.authorship: Independent CC0 course exposition with identified component reuse and human scholarly credit; no research novelty claim.

units.title: Covariant derivatives and curvature
units.topics: Differentiating fields under local changes of frame; connection matrices; curvature; gauge covariance; Bianchi identity.
units.learning_outcome: Derive local transformation laws and calculate the entire curvature of a specified connection.

units.title: Bundles, parallel transport and holonomy
units.topics: Local trivializations and transition functions; principal and associated bundles; transport along paths; holonomy; Wilson loops.
units.learning_outcome: Relate local formulas to a global connection and construct gauge-invariant loop observables.

units.title: The Yang-Mills action and field equations
units.topics: Variational principles; invariant metrics; coupling constants; Euler-Lagrange equations; boundary terms; pure theory and coupling to matter.
units.learning_outcome: Derive the field equations from the stated action while retaining the group, signature, units and boundary assumptions.

units.title: Constraints, initial data and energy
units.topics: Temporal and other gauges; Gauss constraint; admissible Cauchy data; stress-energy; conservation and flux.
units.learning_outcome: Identify valid initial data and derive the corresponding energy and constraint identities.

units.title: Local and global classical evolution
units.topics: Fourier and Sobolev preparation; local well-posedness; gauge control; finite propagation; finite-energy global results in 3+1 dimensions.
units.learning_outcome: State a classical existence theorem with its exact hypotheses and understand the estimates that enter its proof.

units.title: Euclidean Yang-Mills and instantons
units.topics: Euclidean signature; self-duality; topological charge; energy bounds; instantons and moduli; the relation to four-manifold geometry.
units.learning_outcome: Recognize the different analytical questions posed by elliptic Euclidean equations and Lorentzian time evolution.

units.title: From oscillators to quantum fields
units.topics: Hilbert spaces; observables; self-adjoint Hamiltonians; oscillators; free fields; distributions; vacuum and correlation functions.
units.learning_outcome: Distinguish a classical field configuration from a quantum state and calculate basic spectral and correlation examples.

units.title: Gauge symmetry in the quantum theory
units.topics: Physical states and constraints; gauge fixing; perturbative path integrals; Faddeev-Popov ghosts; Ward identities; an introduction to BRST.
units.learning_outcome: Identify the physical quantities a quantization procedure must preserve and the scope of a perturbative calculation.

units.title: Renormalization and asymptotic freedom
units.topics: Regularization; renormalized parameters; scale dependence; beta functions; asymptotic freedom; the limits of perturbation theory.
units.learning_outcome: Follow the relation between regulator parameters and physical scales and state what a perturbative result establishes.

units.title: Yang-Mills theory on a lattice
units.topics: Links and plaquettes; compact-group Haar integration; Wilson action; gauge-invariant observables; transfer matrices and Hamiltonian descriptions.
units.learning_outcome: Construct a finite regulator model and track the relation between its variables and continuum geometry.

units.title: Strong coupling, simulations and their errors
units.topics: Strong-coupling methods; Monte Carlo sampling; lattice spacing; finite volume; statistical and systematic errors; continuum extrapolation.
units.learning_outcome: Read a lattice result with its regulator, error analysis and applicable regime intact.

units.title: Spectra, mass gaps and confinement
units.topics: Vacuum subtraction; spectral measures; correlation decay; mass extraction; Wilson-loop criteria; the differences between gap and confinement questions.
units.learning_outcome: State precisely which observable and limiting procedure a spectral or confinement claim concerns.

units.title: Continuum limits and reconstruction
units.topics: Infinite volume and removal of the ultraviolet regulator; correlation distributions; positivity; locality; Euclidean and Wightman frameworks; reconstruction.
units.learning_outcome: List the data and estimates needed to turn a regulated calculation into a continuum quantum theory.

units.title: The established research landscape and open problems
units.topics: Classical PDE, geometric gauge theory, perturbative results, lattice evidence and constructive approaches; lower-dimensional comparisons; the four-dimensional existence and mass-gap problem.
units.learning_outcome: Place a paper in the literature by its exact model, dimension, assumptions, proof status and contribution.

entry_preparation: Basic algebra, elementary calculus and matrix arithmetic, with a preparatory review. Geometry, PDE analysis and quantum theory are introduced in stages.
